No other regressions found. steps.json compared with HEAD view by view: only Steps 19, 19c, 20, 20c (camera), 33c (labels), 37 (guides) and 42/42c (camera, ride_beats, carry via, wire_via) changed. findings.fix: Turn in smaller steps where the wire shapes change from one arrangement to the other. In guide.py, TURNING = [between(MODULE_LIFTED, MODULE_HELD, f, _mid_module) for f in (1/3, 1/2, 2/3)], and add a turning_layout() case for the half-way pose: carry the lifted shapes there, then settle them with settled(...) against the held shapes carried back. Extend _stages and the module's ride list to match. The overshoot from blending between carried shapes grows with the turn per beat (about r(1 - cos(angle/2))), so halving the turn per beat cuts the ~7.7 mm to about 2 mm. To keep the step near 6.4 s, the A end's 'lifted' and 'carried over' stops could become one beat. Re-run motioncheck and the ray test from the camera, and tell Lee what is left.

verdicts.reason: The main claim is a known false positive. The '6.4-7.7 mm through every one of its 21 wires' lines are check_caps.py's cap-against-wire test (line 291). That test compares wire points with the carried part's axis-aligned bounding box, not its mesh. The script's own docstring says: 'Large parts carried as riders (the module in Step 42) give false cap-against-wire hits: their box holds the wires.' The wires plug into the module's pins, so they are always inside its box. The same 7.69 mm lines appear in round 2's Step 42c (round2/motion_check.txt), which notes 'Step 42c's cap hits are the module's own box (false)'. The 'up to 6.8 mm into the Nano Board' figure is from the mesh-based test and is real: one dot matrix wire (CLK) at t=0.32. The ~1.4 mm hits mean the wire centres are about 0.8 mm inside the module (wire radius 0.625). Both are in the same middle beat the README already reports as not cured. Both are smaller than before this round: round 2 had the matrix CLK at 7.72 mm into the Nano and several matrix wires 4-7 mm into the Nano and into the Mini-B plug. The 'about 2 mm' estimate for halving the turn is based on the false 7.7 mm figure. The frames at 0.313 and 0.375 show the board edge-on with wires looping round it, as wires plugged into a turning board must. The visible crossings are the bundle crossings already reported.
verdicts.fix: No change needed for the box hits. Optionally, for honesty with Lee, widen the README's 'Not cured' sentence: in the middle third of the turn one dot matrix wire also passes into the Nano Board for a moment. Also make check_caps.py skip the cap-vs-wire box test for a rider that is the module, so the output stops reporting these false hits.
